newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FRANCE SAYS READY TO ACCELERATE EU, NATO EXPANSION.
newsitem.headline: FRANCE SAYS READY TO ACCELERATE EU, NATO EXPANSION.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said on Friday that France was ready to speed up the process of European Union and NATO enlargement and that he backed Czech hopes to join the EU by the year 2000.

"France is determined to support and even accelerate all processes concerning enlargement of the EU and the Atlantic alliance," de Charette told a joint news conference with Czech Foreign Minister Josef Zielenec.
"We consider that it is a strategic choice which is important for European unity, not only for current members but also for candidates," he added.
The Czech Republic, along with Poland and Hungary, are seen as leading candidates to be the first new members of both the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) and the EU.
"I think it would be realistic to talk about the end of our negotiations with the EU at the end of the millenium," Zielenec told the news conference.
When the Czech Republic, which has an association agreement with Brussels, applied to join the EU, Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said full membership by 2000 was realistic.
However, ministers have lately been less precise on dates.
De Charette paid tribute to the Czechs for reaching an accord with Germany meant to help heal the wounds of World War Two ands its aftermath.
The agreement, reached after two year of delicate negotiations, is to be signed in Prague next Tuesday by German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Klaus.
"It is a major event for your country, for Germany and for all Europeans," said de Charette.
In the accord, Bonn expresses its sorrow for the 1938-45 Nazi occupation of the Czech lands and Prague its regret for Czech brutality in the post-war expulsion of ethnic Germans.
It also includes Germany's full backing for the Czechs to join NATO and the EU.
The agreement is seen as an important pre-condition for Czech membership. Germany has been the chief sponsor of post-Communist states joining both groups.
Zielenec said his talks with de Charette had covered a wide range of questions of EU and NATO expansion and that France had offered to help train Czech negotiators.
De Charette, who is due to hold talks with Industry Minister Vladimir Dlouhy on Saturday, said he had also come to prepare for a visit to Prague by French President Jacques Chirac.
